title: Define database schema for all tables
description: Create src/db/schema.ts with Drizzle ORM table definitions for all five tables: batches, prospects, media, sent_emails, and settings. Use sqliteTable from drizzle-orm/sqlite-core. Only use types that map cleanly to both SQLite and Postgres (text, integer, real) for future Supabase migration.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/db/schema.ts` exports all five table definitions: batches, prospects, media, sentEmails, settings
All required fields, types, and constraints are present as specified in the PRD data model
`prospects.status` field accepts all pipeline status values
JSON blob fields (scraped_raw, site_content, etc.) are defined as `text` columns

steps.description: Create src/db/schema.ts with the batches table

steps.details: Add to schema.ts. Include all fields: id, batch_id (FK reference), slug (unique), business_name, industry, location, phone, email, existing_url, notes, status, scraped_raw, scraped_branding, extracted_data, condensed_profile, structure, site_content, site_config, custom_palette (nullable), outreach_sent_at (nullable), outreach_responded_at (nullable), exported_at (nullable), created_at, updated_at. Use `.references(() => batches.id)` for batch_id. Use `.unique()` for slug. Status default: 'pending'.

```ts
export const media = sqliteTable('media', {
  id: text('id').primaryKey(),
  batchId: text('batch_id').notNull().references(() => batches.id),
  filename: text('filename').notNull(),
  slot: text('slot').notNull(),
  industry: text('industry').notNull(),
  path: text('path').notNull(),
  createdAt: integer('created_at').notNull(),
});
```
Include: id, prospect_id (FK), template_id, to_email, from_email, subject, body_html, body_text, status (sent|failed|mock), provider_id (nullable), sent_at.

steps.description: Verify schema compiles and run drizzle-kit generate
steps.details: Run `npx drizzle-kit generate` to produce migration SQL in the `./drizzle/` folder. Confirm the generated SQL contains CREATE TABLE statements for all five tables with the correct columns.

technicalNotes: Use only `text`, `integer`, `real` column types — no SQLite-specific BLOB or JSON types. JSON data is stored as `text` and parsed in application code.
Use camelCase for TypeScript property names (e.g., `batchId`) but snake_case for SQL column names (e.g., `'batch_id'`) — Drizzle handles the mapping.
